messages:
maya: Running the AWQ + GPTQ compatibility bakeoff on Mistral3; seeing intermittent hangs when we route through vLLM + TensorRT-LLM. Repro steps below.
samir: ugh, hangs how — crash, OOM, or stalls?
jia: Stalls. Worker GPUs go to 0% and request queues pile up. No OOM, no SIGSEGV.
omments: infra-bot created task CI-4567 for investigation :spiral_notepad:
maya: Minimal repro command I used:
```bash
python -m experiments.run_bakeoff \
  --model mistral3-8b \
  --quant awq,gptq \
  --runtime vllm,trtllm \
  --batching continuous \
  --cuda 14 --driver 535.86
```
maya: Logs show repeated timeouts inside TensorRT-LLM plugin, then vLLM stops pulling from queue. Sample log excerpt:
```
[trt_plugin] WARN: enqueue failed, cudaStreamWaitEvent returned error 700
[vllm] ERROR: request handler timeout after 300s
```
oliver: error 700 is CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS, right? often driver mismatch or kernel bug.
samir: could be kernel using unsupported PTX for driver. What driver + cuda on the host?
maya: host had CUDA 14.1, nvidia driver 535.86. I repro'd also on a 536 driver and saw same stalls but different sign: `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED` before stall.
jia: Did you try disabling continuous batching? maybe request coalescing triggers a race in the TRT plugin.
maya: Yes — with batching=single the hangs disappeared; throughput obviously drops but stability improved.
oliver: interesting. That points at concurrency sync between vLLM's batching and TRTLLM's stream/event handling.
eva: Any diffs between AWQ and GPTQ runs in terms of failure rate?
maya: AWQ fails ~60% of runs under continuous batching, GPTQ ~10%. AWQ shows more kernel fusion passages in trt logs.
samir: Could be different kernel selection triggers codepaths that use cudaEventRecord/cudaStreamWaitEvent patterns which exposed a bug.
maya: Quick workaround I tried: export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 — makes it deterministic, no hangs but perf tanked. Also tried setting environment var `TRT_DISABLE_IMMEDIATE_SYNC=1` (not official) — seemed to reduce failures but not full fix.
jia: Can you paste the small callstack trace around the WARN line? even a few function names help.
maya: paste:
```
trt_plugin::enqueueTensor -> executeKernel -> cudaStreamWaitEvent -> cudaGetLastError -> <<<error 700>>>
```
oliver: ok. Filing a ticket with TRTL plugin folks, but we should also test with vLLM 0.7 RC; vLLM has a batching refactor in that release.
eva: Also try building TRTLLM with CUDA 15 toolchain? there might be a PTX vs SASS mismatch for certain ops.
samir: Action plan:
- maya: run matrix vs vllm 0.6/0.7 + trtllm built with CUDA 14/15 (small runs) — collect failure counts and tiny perf metrics (p50 latency)
- oliver: reach out to trt-llm plugin owners, include the log + stack + kernel list
- jia: run evals for AWQ/GPTQ profiles to capture accuracy deltas so we can weigh stability vs perf
- eva: try driver 535.xx vs 540.x on a repro node
maya: ack. Starting the matrix now, will push a short artifact with counts to the ticket. current quick numbers: (continuous batching, 50 trials each)
- AWQ + vLLM + TRTLLM (CUDA14, driver535): 31/50 hangs
- GPTQ + vLLM + TRTLLM (same env): 5/50 hangs
- AWQ + vLLM (no TRTLLM): 0/50 hangs
maya: also ran a small eval set: AWQ perplexity +0.45 vs FP16 baseline, GPTQ +0.18. MMLU drop for AWQ ~1.1% absolute on our tiny eval.
samir: good to record; if AWQ is materially better perf but unstable, might need a policy: use AWQ on Dedicated where we can pin runtime (no TRTLLM) or force single batching on shared.
oliver: For triage: attach `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` logs, `nvidia-smi -q` output, and `cuobjdump --dump-lineinfo` of the offending kernel if possible.
maya: will attach to CI-4567. ETA: first matrix results in ~2hrs. ping me for quick access to repro node.
eva: thanks! would be good to also capture token-level latency traces so we can correlate the time when kv-cache flushes happen.
maya: noted. will include traces. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: CI task CI-4567 updated: "quant pipeline interop hangs — collect logs + matrix" assigned to maya, due 2 days.
notes: Thread focuses on intermittent stalls when running AWQ with vLLM + TensorRT-LLM under continuous batching; includes repro command, logs, quick matrix counts, suggested triage plan and workarounds.
